IR.rationale: A steepening curve signals improving growth and reflation expectations, which raise expected demand for industrial commodities and support commodity returns.

B.rationale: Strong high-yield returns with stable Baa spreads describe easy credit and risk appetite. Commodity futures load on this cyclical risk-on state, and slow-moving capital lets it persist into subsequent weeks.

V.rationale: Elevated commodity-specific implied volatility marks states where hedging pressure and risk premia in commodity futures are high, so the expected compensation for bearing commodity risk is larger.

AP.rationale: Emerging-market equities price expected demand from the marginal commodity consumers. Their strength tends to lead or accompany commodity price gains.

ST.rationale: Equity cross-sectional style factors have no clear mechanism linking them to commodity index returns, so the group is left out.

FX.rationale: Commodity-currency strength with a non-rising dollar is the classic commodity-supportive FX state. Commodity currencies have been documented to anticipate commodity prices, and a weaker dollar raises dollar-denominated commodity prices.

COM.rationale: Commodity futures display time-series momentum, so recent strength in the broad basket predicts continued gains over weeks to months.

MC.rationale: Rising breakevens under loose financial conditions describe a reflationary, demand-driven environment in which commodities typically perform well.

ENDG.rationale: Index-level time-series momentum: recent outperformance relative to its own history tends to persist at horizons up to a quarter.

IR.rationale: Abrupt rises in short rates signal monetary tightening surprises. These move the dollar and carry costs and can unsettle commodity markets.

B.rationale: Widening spreads with weak high-yield returns mark deteriorating credit and funding conditions. Speculators then deleverage, raising subsequent commodity volatility.

V.rationale: Option-implied volatility contains forward-looking information beyond lagged realised variance. High energy and gold implied vols together flag a commodity-wide high-uncertainty regime.

AP.rationale: Equity sell-offs raise risk aversion and margin pressure across asset classes, a leverage- and feedback-type effect that spills into commodity volatility.

ST.rationale: Momentum drawdowns occur in turbulent, panic-and-rebound markets, so weak momentum returns flag an unstable risk regime.

FX.rationale: Yen appreciation together with Australian-dollar weakness is a carry-unwind, risk-off signature, and it precedes broader cross-asset turbulence including in commodities.

COM.rationale: Commodity price declines tend to be followed by higher volatility, reflecting asymmetric volatility and forced liquidation by leveraged holders.

MC.rationale: High financial stress tightens funding and limits arbitrage capital, which amplifies price moves in commodity futures.

ENDG.rationale: Volatility is highly persistent with long memory, so elevated recent variance relative to history carries information beyond the short lag.

IR.rationale: Rising short rates combined with curve flattening describe hawkish tightening that weakens expected demand and strengthens the dollar, raising crash risk for commodities.

B.rationale: Credit deterioration signals growth scares and deleveraging, the setting in which commodity prices suffer their largest declines.

V.rationale: When commodity and equity implied volatility are both elevated, the left tail is fat and correlated liquidation is likely.

AP.rationale: Weak emerging-market equities signal falling demand expectations from the main commodity consumers and capital outflows from commodity exporters.

ST.rationale: No credible mechanism ties equity style factors to commodity left-tail risk, so the group is left out.

FX.rationale: A surging dollar with weak commodity currencies is the classic risk-off, commodity-bearish FX state preceding large commodity drawdowns.

COM.rationale: Negative trend in the broad basket raises the odds of further large losses, through time-series momentum and higher subsequent volatility.

MC.rationale: Financial stress coupled with falling inflation expectations describes a deflationary shock, under which commodities have their worst outcomes.

ENDG.rationale: Weak recent index performance signals a downtrend and an elevated-volatility state, both of which raise the probability of a further large loss.

IR.rationale: Curve steepening reflects reflationary growth expectations, which favour strong upside moves in commodity prices.

B.rationale: Strong EM sovereign bonds, heavily exposed to commodity exporters, together with stable US credit spreads mark risk-on conditions conducive to commodity rallies.

V.rationale: High commodity-specific uncertainty without broad equity panic points to supply-side risk. Such shocks can produce sharp upside commodity moves.

AP.rationale: Emerging-market equity strength signals rising demand from commodity-intensive economies, raising the chance of strong commodity rallies.

ST.rationale: Equity style factors offer no clear mechanism for commodity upside tails, so the group is left out.

FX.rationale: Dollar weakness with strong commodity currencies is the FX state most associated with broad commodity rallies.

COM.rationale: Positive trend in commodities, via time-series momentum, raises the probability of continued outsized gains.

MC.rationale: Rising inflation expectations accompany commodity-price upswings and a reflationary demand environment.

ENDG.rationale: Strong recent index performance signals momentum that raises the odds of further large gains.
